response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.SEX) SELECT sex, cnt AS test_records, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM g) AS fraction_of_total, cnt - (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) FROM g) AS above_average FROM g WHERE cnt > (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) FROM g)

assumptions.assumption: Records are matched to patients with an inner join on ID. Each Laboratory row counts as one test record. The empty-string SEX is its own group because it is a distinct value in GROUP BY.
A NULL SEX, if any exists, forms its own group, as GROUP BY does by default. It counts toward the number of groups, the per-group average and the total.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude patients whose SEX is NULL, so only groups with a non-NULL sex value (including the empty string) are considered.
alternatives.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.SEX) SELECT sex, cnt AS test_records, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM g) AS fraction_of_total, cnt - (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) FROM g) AS above_average FROM g WHERE cnt > (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) FROM g)
